titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 25/2019 (އާމްދަނީން ޓެކްސް ނެގުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް 2 ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This is the second amendment to the Income Tax Act. When a Maldivian business pays a foreign (non-resident) contractor, it must now hold back 10% of the payment as tax. For contractors with no permanent base in the Maldives, that 10% becomes their full and final tax on that income, so no further tax return or deductions apply to it. The bill also rewrites who counts as a 'non-resident contractor'.
whyItMatters: Foreign firms paid for goods or services in the Maldives keep less of each payment, and local businesses that hire them must withhold and pass 10% to the tax authority. The stated aim is fairer competition for Maldivian businesses.
keyProvisions: Section 55(b) rewritten: anyone doing business in the Maldives who pays a non-resident contractor must withhold 10% of the payment as withholding tax.

New section 27(n): for non-residents without a permanent establishment in the Maldives, the amount withheld is treated as the full tax due on that income; it is left out of taxable income and no related deductions are allowed.
New section 27(r): sections 43 and 44 of the Act apply only in a way consistent with the new 27(n).
New section 55(b-1): if a payment could fall under both 55(a) and 55(b), it is treated as a 55(b) contractor payment.

Section 55(n)(3) redefines 'non-resident contractor' as a non-resident who, other than as an employee, supplies goods or services in the Maldives, or provides or permits another party's goods or services to be supplied here, under a contract or arrangement.
Takes effect on the date it is published in the Government Gazette after ratification.
whoIsAffected: Foreign contractors paid for work or supplies in the Maldives, and the Maldivian businesses and bodies that pay them.
statedReasons: The Final Bill has no reasons section. The original bill's stated reason was to create a fair, competitive environment between Maldivian businesses and non-resident contractors by raising the withholding on payments to non-resident contractors from 5% to 10% and making it their full tax.
